parts.text:
```yaml
- id: DR-01
  requirement: >
    The service must isolate each operating company's data so that a company's
    fleet, jobs, sites, charging pads, and operational problems are visible and
    accessible only to that company and never exposed to competing companies.
- id: DR-02
  requirement: >
    The service must prevent airspace desk personnel from viewing or accessing
    any individual operating company's private operations, fleet, jobs, sites,
    or problems.
- id: DR-03
  requirement: >
    The service must allow fleet technicians to register new drones into their
    company's fleet (supporting fleets of several hundred drones per company)
    and record each drone's manufacturer, model, payload capacity, flight range
    on a full battery, installed sensors, charging connector type, and home site.
- id: DR-04
  requirement: >
    The service must allow fleet technicians to retire old drones from their
    company's fleet so that retired drones can no longer be assigned to flights
    or operations.
- id: DR-05
  requirement: >
    The service must allow fleet technicians to take a drone out of service for
    repairs and servicing, and to return the drone to active service when
    repairs are complete.
- id: DR-06
  requirement: >
    The service must allow fleet technicians to register and set up charging
    pads at their company's sites (supporting several dozen charging pads per
    company), including specifying the charging connector type for each pad.
- id: DR-07
  requirement: >
    The service must allow fleet technicians to assign a drone to a charging
    pad to charge only if the charging pad belongs to the same company and has
    the exact same charging connector type as the drone, because connector
    types are not interchangeable and companies never lend pads to other
    companies.
- id: DR-08
  requirement: >
    The service must allow dispatchers to plan flights by manually selecting
    the specific drone and the flight path (corridors) for the flight, and the
    service must never automatically select or assign a drone or a flight path
    on behalf of a dispatcher.
- id: DR-09
  requirement: >
    The service must allow a dispatcher to sign off a planned flight before it
    departs, and allow a dispatcher to call off a flight when needed.
- id: DR-10
  requirement: >
    The service must handle concurrent flight planning by multiple dispatchers
    within the same company so that popular drones and busy sites or resources
    cannot be conflictingly double-booked when flights are planned and signed
    off.
- id: DR-11
  requirement: >
    The service must process incoming drone telemetry and flight reports in a
    way that tolerates patchy radio coverage and mid-flight drone software
    restarts—specifically handling reports that arrive late, arrive out of
    chronological order, arrive multiple times (duplicates), or are missing—without
    corrupting the tracked state of the flight or drone.
- id: DR-12
  requirement: >
    The service must track actual reported battery levels during flight rather
    than relying solely on planned battery consumption, accounting for faster
    battery drain caused by cold or wind.
- id: DR-13
  requirement: >
    The service must allow the airspace desk to maintain a shared airspace
    picture visible to all customer companies, consisting of the network of
    flight corridors between sites, the zones that group those corridors, and
    airspace closures announced by the authorities.
- id: DR-14
  requirement: >
    The service must allow the airspace desk to enter new airspace closures and
    amend existing closures announced by the authorities, including closures
    that take effect immediately while drones from one or more companies are
    already in the air.
- id: DR-15
  requirement: >
    When an airspace closure is entered or amended, the service must immediately
    identify affected planned and in-flight operations so that dispatchers are
    alerted when their active or planned flights are impacted by the closure.
- id: DR-16
  requirement: >
    When the airspace desk enters or amends an airspace closure, the service
    must provide the airspace desk with an aggregated measure of how much
    disruption the closure caused across all customer companies without
    revealing any individual company's identity or private operational details.
- id: DR-17
  requirement: >
    The service must persist flight, fleet, and airspace state durably so that
    server updates, restarts during working hours, or unexpected server crashes
    do not lose or corrupt the state of active flights in the air, planned
    flights, fleet records, or airspace closures.
```
